title: What physical good includes
source_text: III. Ad bonum autem istud quod Physicum dicitur, pertinet tum natura ipsa, & ejus facultates, tum commoda & dona quaecunque illam extra rationem virtutis perficiunt, cujuscunque tandem generis sint, sive ex principiis naturae oriantur, sive supra naturam a Deo concedantur. Ac propterea hoc bonum non dicitur bonum Physicum, seu naturae, ut per id opponatur bono supernaturali, sed solum ut opponatur bono morali, quod modo descriptum est.
pass_a_gloss: III. But to that good which is called Physical belongs both nature itself and its faculties, and whatever advantages and gifts perfect it outside the notion of virtue, of whatever kind at length they be, whether they arise from the principles of nature, or are granted by God above nature. And therefore this good is not called physical good, or of nature, so that by it it be opposed to supernatural good, but only so that it be opposed to moral good, which has just been described.
pass_b_english: Physical good includes nature itself and its faculties, and every advantage and gift that perfects nature apart from the character of virtue, of whatever kind, whether it springs from natural principles or is granted by God above nature.
So this good is called physical, or the good of nature, not to set it against supernatural good, but only to set it against moral good as just described.

lemmas.gloss: perfect it outside the notion of virtue

lemmas.gloss: or are granted by God above nature

lemmas.gloss: but only so that it be opposed to moral good

choices.why: The Schools' term for the good that earns praise or reward and makes a man good without qualification; kept as 'moral good', with the narrower Roman sense explained in the text.
